electric-violet.$description: Electric Violet — Brand accent — used sparingly for emphasis moments, selected icon strokes, and tag punctuation; the only saturated color in the system creates instant focus when it appears against the warm neutral canvas

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Card surfaces, product screenshot backgrounds, inverted button text

canvas-cream.$description: Canvas Cream — Primary page canvas — the warm off-white that defines the entire surface temperature; every screen lives on this tone

linen.$description: Linen — Secondary surface for sectioned blocks, elevated cards, and alternating content bands — one step warmer than canvas

stone.$description: Stone — Decorative texture wash, large background fields, subtle warmth blocks

hairline.$description: Hairline — Hairline borders, dividers, input outlines, nav separators — the warm border tone that never feels cold

ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, headings, body copy — slightly softer than pure black for comfortable reading on cream

carbon.$description: Carbon — Dark supporting neutral for text, icons, and strong contrast. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

iron.$description: Iron — Secondary text, supporting copy, muted descriptions

graphite.$description: Graphite — Tertiary text, helper copy, less-prominent body

smoke.$description: Smoke — Disabled state text, placeholder copy, very muted labels

ash.$description: Ash — Muted headings in secondary contexts, low-emphasis text

silver.$description: Silver — Icon strokes in resting state, low-emphasis glyphs

saans.$description: Primary typeface for everything — display headlines at weight 300 (80px/54px/40px), headings at 300 (32px/24px), body at 400 (16px/20px). The 300-weight display is the signature: most brands shout at 700–800, Intercom whispers at 300 and achieves authority through restraint. Use weight 400 only for body and supporting text where readability is paramount.

saansmono.$description: Monospace labeling system — nav micro-labels, tab labels, tag chips, section metadata. Always paired with wide positive tracking to function as typographic badges. The 100em spacing on 12px is a 'shout' weight for the smallest text, making it readable as a label rather than body copy.

serrif.$description: Editorial counterpoint — appears in select body paragraphs and pull quotes at 16px/300 to add a humanist, almost literary quality. The contrast of serif at 300 against Saans display at 300 creates the magazine-spread rhythm that defines Intercom's voice.

mediumll.$description: Secondary utility face for small UI labels and nav micro-copy where a condensed, tight feel is needed. Used sparingly — only 15 occurrences.
